items.title: Three Kinds of Concentration (Part 2): Uncontaminated — Entering Without Deliberating the Marks

items.zh: 云何無漏靜慮等定？謂如有一，是隨信行，或隨法行，薄塵行類。彼或先時於四聖諦已入現觀，或復正修現觀方便。彼先所由諸行狀相，入初靜慮或所餘定，今於此行、此狀、此相不復思惟。
items.en: What is uncontaminated dhyāna-and-concentration? Someone who is a follower-by-faith or a follower-by-Dharma, of the thin-defilement type, who has either already entered the direct realisation of the four noble truths, or is now cultivating the means towards it. The marks of practice, of state, and of object by which he formerly entered the first dhyāna or another concentration — these marks of practice, state, and object he now no longer contemplates.

items.title: How an Absorption Is Made Uncontaminated: Insight Layered onto Stillness

items.zh: 然於諸色乃至識法思惟如病、如癰等行；於有為法心生厭惡，怖畏制伏；於甘露界繫念思惟；如是方能入無漏定。
items.en: Yet he contemplates form up through mind-objects as a disease, as a boil, and so on; towards the conditioned his mind gives rise to revulsion, dread, and subdual; and he fixes his mindfulness upon the deathless realm — only thus is he able to enter the uncontaminated concentration.

items.title: Four Trajectories of Concentration: Falling Back, Staying Put, Advancing, and Penetrating

items.zh: 復次，云何順退分定？謂有鈍根，下劣欲解，勤精進故，入初靜慮或所餘定；於喜、於樂、於勝功德不堪忍故，從靜慮退。如如暫入諸定差別，如是如是還復退失，乃至未善調練諸根。云何順住分定？謂有中根，或利根性，彼唯得聞諸定功德，廣說如前愛味相應。於所得定唯生愛味，不能上進，亦不退下。
items.en: Furthermore, what is retrogression-prone concentration? [The practice of] one with dull faculties and inferior aspiration and understanding who, being diligent, enters the first dhyāna or another concentration, but — unable to bear its joy, its bliss, or its supreme merit — falls back from the dhyāna. Just as he momentarily enters the various concentrations, so does he fall from them again, so long as he has not well tempered his faculties. What is stability-prone concentration? [The practice of] one with middling or sharp faculties who has heard only the merits of the concentrations, as above for the relish-associated; towards the concentration attained he gives rise only to relish, unable to advance yet not falling back.

items.zh: 云何順勝分定？謂有亦聞出離方便，於所得定不生喜足。是故於彼不生愛味，更求勝位；由此因緣，便得勝進。云何順決擇分定？謂於一切薩迦耶中，深見過患；由此因緣，能入無漏。又諸無漏名決擇分。極究竟故。猶如世間珠瓶等物，已善簡者名為決擇。自此已後無可擇故。此亦如是。過此更無可簡擇故，名決擇分。
items.en: What is advancement-prone concentration? [The practice of] one who has also heard the means of release and gives rise to no contentment with the concentration attained; therefore he gives rise to no relish for it but seeks a higher station, and thereby gains advancement. What is penetration-prone concentration? Deeply seeing the faults in all self-embodiment, and by this able to enter the uncontaminated. Moreover, all the uncontaminated is called "penetration," being utterly final — just as, among worldly gems and vessels, what has been well sorted is called "decided," since after that there is nothing more to sort; so too here, since beyond this there is nothing more to discriminate, it is called "penetration."

items.title: Entering the Attainments Without Interval, and by Leaping

items.zh: 復次，云何無間入諸等至？謂如有一，得初靜慮乃至有頂，然未圓滿清淨鮮白。先順次入乃至有頂，後逆次入至初靜慮。
items.en: Furthermore, what is entering the attainments without interval? Someone who has attained the first dhyāna up to the peak of existence, but not yet perfectly, purely, and brightly. He first enters in forward sequence up to the peak of existence, and afterwards in reverse sequence down to the first dhyāna.

items.zh: 復次，云何超越入諸等至？謂即於此已得圓滿清白故，從初靜慮無間超入第三靜慮，第三無間超入空無邊處，空處無間超入無所有處。乃至廣說逆超亦爾。以極遠故，無有能超第三等至。唯除如來，及出第二阿僧企耶諸大菩薩。彼隨所欲入諸定故。
items.en: Furthermore, what is entering the attainments by leaping? Because he has now attained the perfect and pure [mastery], from the first dhyāna he leaps without interval into the third dhyāna, from the third leaps into the sphere of infinite space, and from the space-sphere leaps into the sphere of nothingness; and, as explained at length, reverse-leaping is likewise. Because [the further stations] are too remote, none can leap into a third attainment [two levels off] — except a Tathāgata and the great bodhisattvas who have passed the second incalculable eon, for they enter the concentrations however they wish.

items.title: Permeation-Cultivation: Interleaving the Contaminated and the Uncontaminated for Mastery

items.zh: 復次，云何薰修靜慮？謂如有一，已得有漏及與無漏四種靜慮，為於等至得自在故，為受等至自在果故，長時相續入諸靜慮。有漏、無漏更相間雜。乃至有漏無間無漏現前，無漏無間還入有漏，當知齊此薰修成就。若於是處、是時、是事欲入諸定，即於此處、此時、此事能入諸定，是名於諸等至獲得自在。
items.en: Furthermore, what is permeation-cultivation of dhyāna? Someone who has attained both the contaminated and the uncontaminated four dhyānas, in order to gain mastery over the attainments and to receive the fruit of that mastery, enters the dhyānas continuously over a long time, the contaminated and the uncontaminated alternating with each other — up to: the contaminated immediately followed by the uncontaminated made present, the uncontaminated immediately re-entering the contaminated. Know that at just this point the permeation-cultivation is accomplished. If, at whatever place, time, and object he wishes to enter the concentrations, he can there and then enter them, this is called gaining mastery over the attainments.

items.zh: 等至自在果者，謂於現法樂住轉更明淨。又由此故，得不退道。又淨修治解脫、勝處及遍處等勝品功德能引之道。若有餘取而命終者，由此因緣，便入淨居。
items.en: The fruit of mastery over the attainments is this: the pleasant abiding in this very life grows ever brighter and purer. By this too he gains the non-retrogressing path. And he purifies the path that can elicit the supreme qualities — the [eight] liberations, the [eight] masteries, the [ten] totalities, and the rest. And if he dies with a remaining grasping, by this cause he enters the Pure Abodes.

items.title: How Dhyāna-Cultivation Shapes Rebirth — and Why the Bliss Is the Same in Either Realm

items.zh: 由軟中上品修諸靜慮，有差別故，於一切處受三地果。如前有尋有伺地已廣分別。修習無尋唯伺三摩地故，得為大梵。由軟、中、上、上勝、上極品薰修力故，生五淨居。
items.en: By cultivating the dhyānas in soft, middling, and superior grades — because of this difference — one receives in each case the fruit of the three levels [of that dhyāna's heaven], as already analysed at length in the Ground With Applied-and-Sustained Thought. By cultivating the concentration of only-sustained-thought, one becomes a Great Brahmā. And by the force of permeation-cultivation in the soft, middling, superior, super-superior, and utmost grades, one is reborn in the Five Pure Abodes.

items.zh: 當知因修清淨靜慮定故，生靜慮地，不由習近愛味相應。既生彼已，若起愛味，即便退沒；若修清淨，還生於彼。或生下定，或進上定，先於此間修得定已，後往彼生。何以故？非未離欲得生彼故，非諸異生未修得定能離欲故。又非此間及在彼處入諸等至樂有差別，唯所依身而有差別。
items.en: One should know that it is by cultivating pure dhyāna-concentration that one is reborn in the dhyāna grounds, not by resorting to relish-associated [concentration]. Having been reborn there, if one gives rise to relish one falls away; if one cultivates purity, one is reborn there again — either reborn in a lower concentration or advancing to a higher. One must first, here [in the desire realm], cultivate and attain the concentration, and afterwards go to be reborn there. Why? Because one who has not left desire cannot be reborn there, and no ordinary being who has not cultivated and attained the concentration can leave desire. Moreover, the bliss of entering the attainments here or there is no different; the difference is only in the supporting body.

items.title: Gathering the Essentials of the Scriptures: The Eight Liberations

items.zh: 復次，已說修習作意相差別。云何攝諸經宗要？謂八解脫等。如經廣說。八解脫者，謂如前說有色觀諸色等。前七解脫，於已解脫生勝解故，名為解脫；第八解脫，棄背想受，故名解脫。
items.en: Furthermore, the cultivation of attention on the marks and their distinctions having been explained, what is the gathering of the essentials of the scriptures? It is the eight liberations and so on, as the scriptures explain at length. The eight liberations are, as stated before, "having form, one contemplates forms," and the rest. The first seven liberations are called "liberation" because one generates a firm conviction towards what is already liberated; the eighth liberation is called "liberation" because it casts away perception and feeling.

blocks.text: Today's reading explains how worldly concentration becomes uncontaminated, describes four directions a concentration can take, and discusses advanced practices: entering absorptions without interval, leaping between them, and "permeating" contaminated with uncontaminated absorption. It ends by explaining how dhyāna practice shapes rebirth.

An uncontaminated practitioner "no longer contemplates" the marks of practice, of state, and of object, and fixes mindfulness on "the deathless realm". Venerable Miào Jìng on "state": the bodily sensations that precede absorption; trembling, he warns, "is mostly illness, not the sign of the first dhyāna". Master Cháng Bǎi, citing Zhìyǐ: sensations that begin at the crown tend to lead to regression; those that begin at the soles tend to lead into the first dhyāna.

One cannot fix the mind on the deathless directly, Venerable Miào Jìng says: "it must go through the conditioned, the five aggregates." Insight into the aggregates, practised within the dhyāna, makes the absorption uncontaminated: insight layered onto stillness.

A concentration may **fall back**, **stay put**, **advance**, or **penetrate** (lead to insight). One with dull faculties, "unable to bear its joy and bliss", falls back. Venerable Miào Jìng: like someone who suddenly gets rich, can't handle it, and loses everything. One who has heard the means of release and is not content with what he has attained advances. One who sees the faults of the whole self-existence penetrates.

Master Cháng Bǎi on the Yogācāra reading of *satkāya*: 薩 means "shifting", "neither definitely existent nor non-existent". The uncontaminated is like sorted gems: "after this there is nothing more to sort."

One whose attainments are not yet perfect enters them in sequence, forwards and back. Venerable Miào Jìng: like reciting a long mantra not yet fluent, going over it again and again. Only a Tathāgata and great bodhisattvas can "leap" two levels at once.

**Permeation-cultivation** (熏修) alternates contaminated and uncontaminated absorption. Master Cháng Bǎi: "thirty minutes of contaminated concentration, then five of uncontaminated, then thirty more", the uncontaminated gradually increasing (Day 24's pure abodes). Its fruits: happiness here and now grows brighter, and the path no longer regresses.

Cultivating the intermediate dhyāna, one may become Great Brahmā. The five pure abodes are only for noble ones. Rebirth above comes not from relish but from having accomplished the concentration, and "one must first, here, cultivate and attain the concentration", because no ordinary being leaves desire without it. Venerable Miào Jìng: entering form-realm absorption here, "your bliss equals that of the gods there"; only the body differs.

The treatise now gathers "the essentials of the scriptures", beginning with the eight liberations. "The first seven are called liberations because one generates firm conviction towards what is already liberated; the eighth casts away perception and feeling." Tomorrow's reading takes them one by one.

quiz.q: The uncontaminated practitioner "no longer contemplates" the marks of practice, state, and object. What is "state," and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say "no longer" means?
options: "state" is the eight bodily sensations (shaking is usually illness, not dhyāna); "no longer contemplating" means switching from the contaminated method to the uncontaminated aspects — disease, boil, and so on
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Such shaking is mostly illness, not the sign of the first dhyāna"; "now he no longer practices contaminated dhyāna but uncontaminated — how?" The translation's "no longer needs to" implies natural ease, unlike the lecture's "switching methods" (logged).

quiz.q: Entering the uncontaminated requires "fixing mindfulness on the deathless realm." How, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: not directly — only through the conditioned five aggregates; practising mindfulness within dhyāna makes the absorptions uncontaminated
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "You can't fix the mind directly on the deathless realm; it must go through the conditioned — the five aggregates"; "practising the four foundations of mindfulness within dhyāna turns the absorptions uncontaminated." Nectar, the gods' elixir, symbolises nirvāṇa.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, whose is the retrogression-prone concentration?
options: one with dull faculties and inferior aspiration who, unable to bear the joy, bliss, and merit, falls back
quiz.why: "One with dull faculties and inferior aspiration who, being diligent, enters the first dhyāna … but — unable to bear its joy, its bliss, or its supreme merit — falls back." Venerable Miào Jìng: 欲解 is wish plus understanding; the translation gives only "aspiration."

quiz.q: Penetration-prone concentration sees the faults of all 薩迦耶 (self-embodiment). How does Master Cháng Bǎi say the Yogācāra school renders 薩?
options: as "shifting" — neither fixed as existent nor nonexistent, seemingly real — hence "view of the shifting body"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The Mahāyāna Yogācāra school takes 薩 as 'shifting' — 'neither definitely existent nor nonexistent, seemingly but not really existent' — and so renders this view 'the view of a shifting body.'" Without cutting self-view, even dhyāna leads back into existence.

quiz.q: In leaping entry, who can leap into a "third" attainment two levels away?
options: only a Tathāgata and great bodhisattvas past the second incalculable eon, who enter concentrations at will
quiz.why: "Because the further stations are too remote, none can leap … — except a Tathāgata and the great bodhisattvas who have passed the second incalculable eon, for they enter the concentrations however they wish." Master Cháng Bǎi: the second eon covers the first through seventh grounds; the third, the eighth and above.

quiz.q: Permeation-cultivation alternates contaminated and uncontaminated absorption. How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe it concretely?
options: thirty minutes contaminated, five uncontaminated, thirty contaminated again — the uncontaminated gradually increasing, the contaminated decreasing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "For instance, thirty minutes of contaminated concentration, then five of uncontaminated, then thirty more contaminated — the uncontaminated slowly increasing, the contaminated decreasing." The text: when they alternate without interval, permeation is accomplished.

quiz.q: Why must one first attain concentration in the desire realm before being reborn above?
options: one not free of desire cannot be reborn there, and no ordinary being can leave desire without attaining concentration
quiz.why: "One must first, here, cultivate and attain the concentration, and afterwards go to be reborn there. Why? Because one who has not left desire cannot be reborn there, and no ordinary being who has not cultivated and attained the concentration can leave desire." Venerable Miào Jìng: in one moment of mind, desire and concentration exclude each other.
